polymarket-2915400.brief: The initiative 'For a restriction on fireworks' is on the 29 November 2026 federal ballot and needs both a popular majority and a majority of cantons (half-cantons count as half). The Federal Council and Parliament recommend No, saying it goes too far because cantons and municipalities can already restrict fireworks (https://www.admin.ch/feuerwerksinitiative); a cross-party No campaign with SVP, FDP and Mitte launched on 6 October (https://www.srf.ch/news/schweiz/verbot-von-boellern-nein-kampagne-gegen-feuerwerksinitiative-lanciert). The National Council rejected the indirect counter-proposal, so the initiative is on the ballot alone (https://www.srf.ch/news/schweiz/verbot-von-boellern-feuerwerksinitiative-kommt-ohne-gegenvorschlag-vors-volk, 2026-06-26). The first SRG/gfs.bern wave (fieldwork 5-18 October, 14,874 voters) found 69% in favour (https://www.srf.ch/news/erste-srg-umfrage-ja-vorteil-fuer-feuerwerksinitiative-meinungen-fast-gemacht, 2026-10-23). The second wave, published 2026-11-18, says the initiative would have been clearly approved on 7 November, but the percentages were not read (https://www.gfsbern.ch/en/news/2nd-srg-survey-on-the-federal-votes-of-29-november-2026). The final YouGov barometer (fieldwork 2-16 November, 3,013 voters) had 59% yes, 36% no and 5% undecided (https://yougov.com/de-de/artikel/56001-fairness-initiative-bricht-ein-kriegsmaterialgesetz-bleibt-offen-wie-will-die-schweiz-am-29-november-abstimmen). Base rate: only about 9-11% of federal initiatives pass (22 of 192 from 1893 to 2014, 17 of 182 from 1970 to 2020), but those counts come from secondary sources and do not condition on polls this strong. Initiatives typically lose support during the campaign, which the fall from 69% to 59% across pollsters may reflect. The cantonal majority is unpolled, and rural German-speaking cantons are the main risk. A narrower final margin, or a gfs second wave showing a yes lead below about 55%, would lower the chance of passing.

polymarket-7121567.brief: The question settles on the Binance BTC/USDT 1-minute candle closing at 12:00 ET on 2026-11-24 (16:00-16:01 UTC); it needs a close above 58,000, and exactly 58,000 is No. Binance's ticker read about 63,820 on 2026-11-19 around 10:15 UTC (https://api.binance.com/api/v3/ticker/price?symbol=BTCUSDT), about 10% above the threshold. The 2026-11-18 daily close was 63,068.22 (https://api.binance.com/api/v3/klines?symbol=BTCUSDT&interval=1d&limit=3), and price has fallen about 23% from 83,028 on 2026-10-20. The 30-day standard deviation of daily log returns is about 0.023, so the roughly 126 hours left give a one-sigma move near 5.4%, and the gap is about 1.9 sigma. The reference class is every 5-day window of Binance daily closes since 2017-08-17: 3,112 of 3,377 (92.2%) stayed above 0.9089 times the starting close, 96.8% over the last 4 years and 96.3% over the last 2 years. This is unconditional and uses daily closes as a proxy for the settling minute. Different this time: US spot bitcoin ETFs had $2.58 billion of net outflows from Nov 2 to Nov 17, about 87% from IBIT (https://news.bitcoin.com/bitcoin-etf/bitcoin-etfs-lose-2-58b-in-november-with-blackrock-driving-the-exit/, 2026-11-18), and bitcoin slid under 70,000 on Nov 13 with no single trigger (https://investinglive.com/cryptocurrency/bitcoin-dipped-under-70k-first-time-since-august/). No scheduled macro event falls before resolution: the FOMC is on Dec 8-9 and November CPI on Dec 10 (https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/2026-december.htm, https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/cpi.htm). Unknowns include ETF flows after Nov 17, any Nov 18-19 news, and a roughly 46 USD gap between the Binance trade page and the API ticker. A further decline of about 9-10% before Nov 24, for example from continued outflows or a liquidation cascade, would change the answer.
